thesis: The speaker outlines three historical stages of financial advice: the first was the stockbroker model where advisors earned commissions on trades until 1975 deregulation; the second stage involved a shift to mutual funds and independent broker-dealers driven by technology reducing trade costs and the introduction of 12b-1 fees for ongoing revenue. The discussion highlights how technology disrupted the traditional stockbroker business model, forcing the industry to evolve toward new compensation structures and product distributions.
